examples.ko: 초등학교 육 년 동안 개근을 했어요.
examples.en: I had perfect attendance for six years of elementary school.
I went to school even when sick to get the perfect attendance award.
My younger brother has perfect attendance, with no lateness or absences.

examples.ko: 일 년 내내 학교를 개근하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to attend school every day all year.
I had perfect attendance this semester too.
The teacher praised me for having perfect attendance.

explain: 학교에 하루도 빠지지 않고 나온 것을 말해요. '개근하다', '개근상'으로 자주 써요. 반대로 빠진 날은 '결석'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I was happy to get the perfect attendance award.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에 빠지지 않고 나온 학생에게 주는 상이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An award given to students who never missed school.

phrases.example: 중학교 때 삼 년 동안 개근했어요.
phrases.en: I had perfect attendance for three years in middle school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '개근'에 '하다'를 붙여 동사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds 하다 to the noun 개근 to make a verb.

phrases.en: I didn't miss a single day in order to get perfect attendance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개근은 결석이 없다는 뜻이라서 같이 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired, since 개근 means having no absences.

explain_en: It means attending school without missing a single day. It is often used as '개근하다' and '개근상' (perfect attendance award). A day you miss is called '결석'.

examples.en: I received the keys on the day I paid the balance.

examples.ko: 공사 대금을 다 치른 뒤에야 열쇠를 넘겨받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only take over the keys after paying the full construction cost.
I took over the duties from my senior and am working on them.
I decided to take over my father's shop.
Once you receive the documents, please check them right away.

examples.ko: 새 담당자가 자료를 아직 넘겨받지 못했어요.
examples.en: The new person in charge hasn't received the materials yet.

explain: 반대말은 '넘겨주다'예요. 일, 재산, 서류, 열쇠처럼 책임이나 물건을 다른 사람에게서 이어받을 때 써요. 받는 사람이 주어이고, 사람에게는 '-에게서'를 써요.

phrases.en: I took over that work from my senior.
phrases.nuance_ko: 업무를 이어받을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for taking over a task.

phrases.en: I haven't received the documents yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받지 못한 상황을 말할 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form for when you haven't received something.

phrases.en: The new person in charge took over the duties.
phrases.nuance_ko: '넘겨받다'와 비슷하지만 회사나 공식적인 자리에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '넘겨받다' but used more in workplaces and formal settings.

explain_en: The opposite is '넘겨주다' (to hand over). It is used when you take over responsibility or things like work, property, documents and keys from someone. The receiver is the subject, and the person you receive from takes '-에게서'.

en: to be achieved (a target, quota or goal is reached)

examples.en: The goal is achieved.
This year's sales target was achieved.
Everyone worked hard, and the plan was accomplished.
Please write the achieved numbers in the table.
At this pace it is hard for the goal to be reached.
There are many things not achieved yet.

explain: '이루다'는 소원과 꿈에도 쓰지만, '달성되다'는 매출, 점수, 목표처럼 숫자로 잴 수 있는 것에 많이 써요. 내가 해내면 '달성하다', 결과로 이루어지면 '달성되다'예요.

phrases.en: The goal has not been achieved yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목표나 숫자를 아직 채우지 못했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the target or number has not yet been reached.

phrases.en: If the goal is achieved, we get a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면'을 붙여 조건을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with '-(으)면' to state a condition.

phrases.en: This year's goal was 100 percent achieved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자로 잴 수 있는 일에 퍼센트와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with percentages for measurable targets.

explain_en: '이루다' also fits wishes and dreams, but '달성되다' is mostly used for things you can measure, such as sales, scores and targets. When you accomplish it yourself it is '달성하다', and when it comes about as a result it is '달성되다'.

examples.en: The new movie was a huge success.
The first show was a big hit, so everyone was happy.
This school festival was a great success.

examples.ko: 작은 가게로 시작했는데 지금은 대성공 사례가 됐어요.
examples.en: It started as a small shop and has now become a big success story.
They say that song is a huge hit overseas too.

examples.ko: 대성공 소식을 듣고 팀원들이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The team members clapped when they heard the news of the big success.

explain: '대성공을 거두다', '대성공이다'처럼 써요. 반대는 '대실패'예요. 그냥 '성공'보다 훨씬 크고 기대 이상일 때 써서, 작은 일에 쓰면 과장처럼 들려요.

phrases.example: 그 가수의 첫 콘서트가 대성공을 거두었어요.
phrases.en: The singer's first concert was a huge success.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대성공'과 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with 대성공.

phrases.en: Today's presentation is a huge success!
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과가 아주 좋을 때 바로 말하는 해요체 서술형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A direct polite statement used when the result is great.

phrases.en: The event ended in great success.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 끝난 뒤 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the outcome once something is over.

explain_en: Common patterns are '대성공을 거두다' and '대성공이다'. The opposite is '대실패'. It is much bigger than plain '성공' and beyond expectations, so using it for small things sounds exaggerated.

examples.en: The construction wraps up this week.
The meeting wrapped up faster than I thought.
If the work wraps up well, let's have a meal together.
This year's project will be finished in December.
I'm relieved the event ended safely.
I still have homework that isn't finished.

explain: '끝나다'는 일이 단순히 끝난 거고, '마무리되다'는 끝을 잘 정리해서 완성되었다는 느낌이에요. 마지막 단계에서 쓰는 말이라 시작한 지 얼마 안 된 일에는 어울리지 않아요. 능동은 '마무리하다'로 '일을 마무리하다', '이야기를 마무리하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I'm relieved that the problem was wrapped up well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝이 좋게 정리되었다는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense that things ended in a good, tidy way.

phrases.en: The construction is in its final stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 거의 끝나 가는 시기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the period when a job is almost finished.

phrases.en: I'll wrap up today's work here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, with the person doing the finishing as the subject.

explain_en: 끝나다 just means something ended; 마무리되다 means it was wrapped up neatly and completed. It is a last-stage word and sounds odd for something just started. The active 마무리하다 is used in '일을 마무리하다' and '이야기를 마무리하다'.

dis.h: gets wrapped up or completed properly

p.n: 마감되다 makes it a deadline or closing time rather than the work being done.

examples.ko: 젊었을 때 공사장에서 막일을 많이 했어요.
examples.en: When I was young, I did a lot of manual labor at construction sites.

examples.ko: 아버지는 막일로 번 돈으로 저를 키우셨어요.
examples.en: My father raised me with money he earned from manual labor.
Even manual labor is fine; I just want to find a job.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 막일을 했더니 온몸이 쑤셔요.
examples.en: I did manual labor all day, so my whole body aches.

examples.ko: 방학 동안 막일을 하며 학비를 모았어요.
examples.en: During vacation I saved up tuition by doing manual labor.
Manual labor is hard, but it is rewarding too.

explain: 특별한 기술 없이 몸으로 하는 거친 일을 가리켜요. 비슷한 말로 '막노동'이 있고, '막일을 하다'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: He earns his living expenses through manual labor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '막일'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A near-synonym of 막일.

phrases.example: 방학 때 막일을 해서 돈을 모았어요.
phrases.en: I saved money by doing manual labor during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '막일'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb phrase with 막일.

phrases.example: 아버지는 막일로 돈을 벌어 가족을 먹여 살리셨어요.
phrases.en: My father earned money through manual labor to support the family.
phrases.nuance_ko: '로'를 붙여 일이 돈 버는 수단임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '로' shows that the work is the means of earning money.
phrases.en_equiv: to earn money by manual labor

explain_en: It refers to rough work done with the body, without special skills. A similar word is '막노동', and people often say '막일을 하다' (to do manual labor).

examples.en: Among the applicants, I got through the interview without trouble.

examples.ko: 이번 시험은 큰 실수 없이 무난히 끝났어요.
examples.en: This exam ended smoothly, without any big mistakes.
I'm adjusting to the new school without any problems.

examples.ko: 준비를 많이 해서 발표를 무난히 마쳤어요.
examples.en: I prepared a lot, so I finished the presentation without trouble.

examples.ko: 이 정도 실력이면 무난히 합격할 수 있어요.
examples.en: With this level of skill, you can pass without difficulty.
The moving preparations went more smoothly than I expected.

explain: '쉽게'와 비슷하지만 '큰 문제 없이 별 탈 없이'라는 느낌이 강해서 통과, 합격, 적응, 진행 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 형용사 '무난하다'는 '무난한 색', '무난한 선택'처럼 평범하고 안전하다는 뜻으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I passed the exam without any trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합격, 통과와 함께 써서 별 어려움 없이 됐다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with passing words to show it went without much difficulty.

phrases.example: 여행이 별 탈 없이 잘 끝났어요.
phrases.en: The trip ended well without any problems.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무난히'와 비슷한 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to 무난히 and more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: Black is a safe choice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '무난하다'를 써서 평범하고 안전한 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the adjective 무난하다 for something ordinary and safe.

explain_en: It's close to '쉽게', but it stresses 'without any big problem', so it goes well with passing, adapting, and proceeding. The adjective '무난하다' is also often used for something plain and safe, as in '무난한 색' or '무난한 선택'.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 실제 이야기를 밑바탕으로 썼어요.
examples.en: This novel was written with a true story as its basis.

examples.ko: 좋은 성적의 밑바탕에는 꾸준한 노력이 있어요.
examples.en: Steady effort lies at the foundation of good grades.
Trust is the foundation of every relationship.

examples.ko: 밑바탕을 먼저 칠하고 그 위에 그림을 그려요.
examples.en: I paint the base layer first and draw on top of it.

examples.ko: 기초 체력이 밑바탕이 되어야 오래 달려요.
examples.en: Basic stamina has to be the foundation for you to run for long.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 슬픔이 밑바탕에 깔려 있어요.
examples.en: Sadness runs underneath this song.

explain: 눈에 보이는 것 아래에 깔려 있는 바탕이라서, 생각이나 감정, 노력 같은 추상적인 것에 많이 써요. '기초'와 비슷하지만 '밑바탕'은 속에 깔려 있는 느낌이 더 강해요. '-을 밑바탕으로 하다'로 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 경험이 제 꿈의 밑바탕이 됐어요.
phrases.en: This experience became the foundation of my dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일의 바탕에서 힘이 되는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that supports a thing at its base.

phrases.example: 그 말 밑바탕에는 사랑이 깔려 있어요.
phrases.en: Love lies underneath those words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 잘 보이지 않는 마음이나 생각을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for feelings or ideas that are not visible on the surface.

phrases.en: You need a solid foundation to improve your skills.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밑바탕'보다 공부나 기술의 기본을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more often than '밑바탕' for the basics of study or skills.

explain_en: It means the base lying beneath what you can see, so it is often used for abstract things like ideas, feelings and effort. It is close to '기초', but '밑바탕' has a stronger sense of something lying underneath. A common pattern is '-을 밑바탕으로 하다' (to be based on).

examples.en: My puppy was sick, so I took it to the vet.

examples.ko: 수의사 선생님이 고양이 예방주사를 놓아 주셨어요.
examples.en: The vet gave my cat its vaccination.

examples.ko: 제 꿈은 동물을 치료하는 수의사가 되는 거예요.
examples.en: My dream is to become a vet who treats animals.

examples.ko: 이 동물병원에는 수의사가 세 명 있어요.
examples.en: This animal hospital has three vets.

examples.ko: 수의사는 말 못 하는 동물의 상태를 잘 살펴야 해요.
examples.en: Vets have to observe carefully the condition of animals that can't speak.

examples.ko: 그 수의사는 동물을 정말 아끼는 분이에요.
examples.en: That vet is someone who really cares about animals.

explain: 사람을 보는 의사는 '의사', 동물을 보는 의사는 '수의사'예요. 병원은 '동물병원'이라고 해요. 부를 때는 보통 '수의사 선생님'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 수의사 선생님이 강아지를 잘 봐 주셨어요.
phrases.en: The vet took good care of my puppy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수의사를 직접 부르거나 높여 말할 때 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way to address or politely refer to a vet.

phrases.en: I want to become a vet someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about dreams or careers.

phrases.en: The vet at the animal hospital examined the cat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 곳과 함께 말하면 어떤 수의사인지 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the workplace makes clear which vet you mean.

explain_en: A doctor for people is 의사, and a doctor for animals is 수의사. The clinic is called 동물병원. When addressing one, people usually say 수의사 선생님.

examples.en: I have to write and hand in the report by tomorrow.
It took two days to write and submit the application.
I wrote down all the answers on the exam paper.
The teacher told us to write and hand in a reflection.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 한 달 만에 소설을 써냈어요.
examples.en: That person wrote out a novel in a month.
If you just write your name and submit, the application is done.

explain: '써서 내다'가 합쳐진 말로, 서류나 답안을 써서 제출한다는 뜻으로 많이 써요. '소설을 써내다'처럼 글을 완성해 내놓는 뜻도 있어요. 그냥 제출만 할 때는 '내다'나 '제출하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Please write your name and hand it in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '써내다'를 풀어서 말한 형태로, 쓰는 일과 내는 일을 따로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spelled-out form of '써내다', treating writing and handing in separately.

phrases.example: 시험 시간이 끝나기 전에 답안지를 써냈어요.
phrases.en: I wrote and handed in my answer sheet before time ran out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험에서 답을 써서 제출할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for writing answers and submitting them in an exam.
phrases.en_equiv: to fill out and submit an answer sheet

phrases.example: 그는 십 년 만에 새 소설을 써냈어요.
phrases.en: He wrote a new novel after ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 끝까지 써서 세상에 내놓았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means finishing a piece of writing and releasing it.

explain_en: It combines '써서 내다' and is often used for writing a document or answer and handing it in. It can also mean completing and producing a piece of writing, as in '소설을 써내다'. For just submitting, use '내다' or '제출하다'.

en: to be completed (made whole, as a product or work)

examples.en: The new building will be completed next year.
At last my painting is finished!
When the puzzle is done, I will take a photo.
This dish is only complete once you add the sauce.
It is a song that is not finished yet.
I emailed the completed report.

explain: '끝나다'와 달리 만드는 것이 제대로 갖춰졌다는 느낌이에요. 그림, 건물, 요리처럼 만드는 대상에 써요. 내가 만들어 낼 때는 '완성하다', 만들던 것이 다 갖춰져 끝날 때는 '완성되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The dish is almost finished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝나기 전에 거의 다 되어 가는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is nearly done but not quite yet.

phrases.en: The painting isn't finished yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만드는 것이 아직 덜 갖춰졌을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used when something is not yet fully put together.

phrases.en: I finished the cake myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 직접 끝까지 만들어 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person makes something all the way to the end.

explain_en: Unlike '끝나다', it says that something being made has come together properly. It fits things you make, such as paintings, buildings and dishes. When you make it yourself you say '완성하다', and '완성되다' describes the thing being made reaching its finished state.

dis.h: finished as a whole product or work

p.n: 완료되다 is for tasks or procedures, so it is odd for a painting.

examples.en: I apply the grammar I learned to real conversations.

examples.ko: 이 레시피를 응용해서 새 요리를 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made a new dish by adapting this recipe.

examples.ko: 기본 동작을 응용하면 어려운 동작도 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you build on the basic moves, you can do hard ones too.
The ability to apply things is built through practice.

examples.ko: 시험에는 배운 내용을 응용해서 푸는 문제가 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Many questions on the test could be solved by applying what we learned.

examples.ko: 수학 공식을 응용할 줄 알아야 해요.
examples.en: You need to know how to apply math formulas.

explain: '적용하다'는 규칙이나 방법을 그대로 가져다 쓰는 것이고, '응용하다'는 원리를 바탕으로 조금 바꿔서 쓰는 것이에요. '활용하다'는 가진 것을 잘 이용한다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Try using the expression you learned in a new way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배운 것을 조금 바꿔서 쓰라고 할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to tell someone to adjust what they learned and use it.

phrases.example: 이 방법은 다른 일에도 응용할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can apply this method to other things too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가능성을 말할 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to talk about what is possible.

phrases.en: The applied problems are too hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배운 내용을 바꿔 푸는 문제를 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for problems that need what you learned in a changed form.

explain_en: '적용하다' means using a rule or method as is; '응용하다' means adjusting it a bit based on the principle. '활용하다' feels more like making good use of what you have.

dis.h: adapt learned knowledge for real-life use

p.n: 응용하다 means adapting what you learned. 적용하다 means putting it directly into effect.

examples.en: It's hard to find laborers during the farming season.

examples.ko: 일꾼들이 점심을 먹고 다시 일을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The workers ate lunch and went back to work.

examples.ko: 그 집 아들은 일 잘하는 일꾼이에요.
examples.en: That family's son is a hard worker.

examples.ko: 이사하는 날 일꾼 세 명이 와 줬어요.
examples.en: Three workers came to help on moving day.
I'm glad the newly hired worker is diligent.
Every vacation I worked as a laborer at a construction site.

explain: 주로 농사, 공사처럼 몸으로 하는 일을 하는 사람에게 써서 사무실 직원에게는 어울리지 않아요. '일 잘하는 일꾼'처럼 칭찬으로도 쓰고, 정치인이 '국민의 일꾼'이라고 자신을 낮추어 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: In spring, many farms are looking for workers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일할 사람을 찾는다는 뜻으로 '일꾼'과 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with the headword, meaning to look for workers.

phrases.example: 우리 마을에는 일 잘하는 일꾼이 많아요.
phrases.en: Our village has many hard-working laborers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칭찬하는 말로 쓸 때 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when using the headword as praise.

phrases.en: During the farming season, there aren't enough hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일꾼'은 사람이고, '일손'은 일하는 사람의 힘이나 인원을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: While the headword is a person, this refers to labor or manpower.

explain_en: It is mainly for people doing physical work such as farming or construction, so it doesn't suit office staff. It can be praise, as in '일 잘하는 일꾼', and politicians sometimes humbly call themselves '국민의 일꾼' (the people's servant).

examples.en: I received an encouragement prize in the writing contest.
I am happy to get even an encouragement prize.

examples.ko: 아쉽게도 대상은 못 받고 장려상에 그쳤어요.
examples.en: Unfortunately I missed the grand prize and ended up with the encouragement prize.

examples.ko: 이번 공모전에서 제 친구가 장려상을 탔어요.
examples.en: My friend won an encouragement prize in this contest.
Winners of the encouragement prize get a book as a gift.

examples.ko: 장려상은 우수상보다 한 단계 낮은 상이에요.
examples.en: The encouragement prize is one level below the excellence prize.

explain: 장려상은 대상, 최우수상, 우수상 다음에 주는 상이에요. 열심히 한 사람을 격려하는 느낌이 있어서 '장려상을 받다'라고 해요. '참가상'은 참여만 해도 받는 상이라서 장려상과 달라요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling won an encouragement prize at the art contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '받다'보다 입말에서 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual spoken alternative to 받다.

phrases.en: The encouragement prize winner went up on the stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상을 받은 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who received the prize.

phrases.en: The judge gave me an encouragement prize.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상을 주는 쪽의 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person giving the prize.

explain_en: 장려상 comes after the grand prize, '최우수상' and '우수상'. It has the feel of encouraging someone who tried hard, and you say '장려상을 받다'. A '참가상' is given just for taking part, so it is different.

examples.en: This movie was produced in Korea.
A new drama will be produced next year.
It's an expensive bag because it's handmade.

examples.ko: 광고는 한 달 동안 제작될 거예요.
examples.en: The ad will be produced over a month.
The posters are being made.
These dolls are not made in a factory.

explain: 영화, 드라마, 광고, 포스터처럼 계획해서 만드는 결과물에 잘 써요. 일상의 음식이나 물건에는 '만들어지다'가 더 자연스러워요. 만드는 사람이 주어이면 '제작하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: A new ad is being produced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 만드는 중이라는 진행의 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the production is in progress right now.

phrases.en: I like dramas produced in Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디에서 누가 만들었는지 밝히며 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form used to say where or by whom something was made.

phrases.en: That movie hasn't been produced yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 만들어지지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something has not been made yet.

explain_en: Good for planned works such as films, dramas, ads and posters. For everyday food and objects, '만들어지다' sounds more natural. If the maker is the subject, use '제작하다'.

dis.h: made as a work: film, show, product

p.n: 생산되다 does not fit a film, which is a creative work rather than mass-made goods.

en: to be promoted; to be advanced

examples.en: I was promoted to section chief this year.
My younger brother will be promoted to sergeant next month.

examples.ko: 열심히 일하면 곧 진급할 수 있을 거예요.
examples.en: If you work hard, you will be promoted soon.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 시험을 잘 봐서 상급반으로 진급했어요.
examples.en: That student did well on the exam and moved up to a higher class.
My salary went up after I was promoted.
My friend didn't get promoted and was very upset.

explain: 회사에서는 보통 '승진하다'를 쓰고, '진급하다'는 군대나 학교처럼 계급·단계가 있는 곳에서 더 자주 써요. 학교에서 다음 학년으로 올라가는 것은 '진급'이고, 상급 학교에 들어가는 '진학'과 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: My older brother was promoted to corporal in the army.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 계급이 올라간 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used to say a rank has gone up.

phrases.en: There is a promotion exam next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계급이나 단계를 올리기 위한 시험을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exam taken to move up a rank or level.

phrases.en: I want to get promoted soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람을 말할 때 '-고 싶다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -고 싶다 to express a wish.

explain_en: In companies 승진하다 is the usual word; 진급하다 is more common where there are ranks or grades, such as the military and schools. Moving up a school grade is 진급, so don't confuse it with 진학 (entering a higher school).

examples.en: The cameraman followed the singer and filmed.
I work as a cameraman at a broadcasting station.

examples.ko: 카메라맨은 무거운 카메라를 어깨에 메고 있어요.
examples.en: The cameraman carries a heavy camera on his shoulder.
I asked the cameraman to film this side.

examples.ko: 현장에는 카메라맨 세 명이 와 있었어요.
examples.en: Three cameramen had come to the scene.
The cameramen rushed quickly to the scene of the accident.

explain: 카메라맨은 방송이나 영상을 찍는 사람을 부를 때 써요. 사진을 찍어 주는 사람은 '사진사'라고 해요. 영화에서는 '촬영감독'이라는 말도 써요.

phrases.en: I want to become a movie cameraman.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to talk about dreams or jobs.

phrases.en: Mr. cameraman, please film over here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 사람을 부르거나 높여서 말할 때 '-님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-님' when you address or politely refer to the cameraman.

phrases.en: A broadcast cameraman came to the stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송을 위해 일하는 카메라맨을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means a cameraman who works for broadcasting.

explain_en: '카메라맨' is used for a person who shoots broadcasts or video. A person who takes photos is a '사진사'. In film the word '촬영감독' is also used.

en: to go to school; to come home from school

examples.en: I commute to school by subway.
My home was far, so I commuted an hour each way.
Many students bike to school.

examples.ko: 기숙사에 살지 않고 집에서 통학할 거예요.
examples.en: I'll commute from home instead of living in the dorm.
I memorized English words while commuting to school.
It's tiring commuting to school every morning.

explain: 집에서 학교까지 오가는 것을 말해요. 직장은 '출근하다', 학교는 '통학하다'로 나눠 써요. '통학 버스', '통학 시간'처럼 합쳐서도 써요.

phrases.en: My home is close, so I go to school by bike.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교통수단 뒤에 '(으)로'를 붙여 어떻게 학교에 가는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '(으)로' after the transport to say how you get to school.
phrases.en_equiv: to commute to school by bike

phrases.en: The commute to school is long, so I'm tired.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집과 학교를 오가는 데 걸리는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The time it takes to travel between home and school.

phrases.en: The school bus comes at eight o'clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 학생을 위해 운행하는 버스를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bus that runs for a school or its students.

explain_en: It means going back and forth between home and school. Korean separates 출근하다 for work from 통학하다 for school. It appears in compounds like 통학 버스 (school bus) and 통학 시간 (commute time to school).

examples.ko: 그 가수는 직접 앨범 프로듀서로 일해요.
examples.en: That singer works as the producer of her own album.
The producer is preparing a new drama.
A producer manages the budget and schedule too.
I met a famous producer and got an autograph.
The producer and the singer chose the song together.
I let the producer hear my song.

explain: 방송에서는 'PD'(피디)라고 줄여 부르는 일이 더 많아요. 영화에서는 연출을 '감독'이 맡고 프로듀서는 제작 전체를 챙기고, 음악에서는 앨범이나 곡 만드는 일을 이끄는 사람에게 써요.

phrases.en: I'm a PD who works at a TV station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송에서는 프로듀서를 'PD'(피디)로 더 많이 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: In broadcasting, producers are more often called PD.

phrases.en: He is a famous music producer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앨범이나 곡 만드는 일을 이끄는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who leads the making of albums or songs.

phrases.en: I want to become a producer later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 이야기할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for talking about dreams or jobs.

explain_en: In broadcasting people more often shorten it to 'PD' (pronounced pi-di). In films the '감독' (director) handles the directing while the producer looks after the whole production, and in music it is the person who leads the making of an album or song.

examples.en: My uncle is a producer at a broadcasting station.
The producer chose the filming location.
I am a college student who dreams of becoming a producer.
The producer manages the program from start to finish.

examples.ko: 그 예능 피디와 인터뷰할 기회가 있었어요.
examples.en: I had a chance to interview that variety show producer.
The producer of this drama came to the set too.

explain: 방송에서 프로그램 제작을 맡은 사람을 가리키고, 'PD'라고 영어로 쓰기도 해요. 앞에 '예능', '드라마'를 붙여 어떤 프로그램인지 말해요.

phrases.en: The variety show PD is preparing a new program.
phrases.nuance_ko: '피디' 앞에 '예능'을 붙여 어떤 프로그램을 만드는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '예능' before '피디' tells you which kind of show the person makes.

phrases.en: The drama PD meets the actors in person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드라마를 만드는 피디를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the producer who makes TV dramas.

phrases.en: My friend is a PD at a broadcasting station.
phrases.nuance_ko: '피디'를 영어 글자로 쓴 모양이에요. 글에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the same word written in English letters, often seen in writing.

explain_en: It refers to the person in charge of making a broadcast program, and it is also written in English as PD. Put 예능 or 드라마 before it to say which kind of program.

examples.ko: 우리 반 친구들은 청소할 때 서로 협동해요.
examples.en: My classmates cooperate when we clean.
The team members worked together and finished a hard task.
Ants carry food by working together.
Working together is faster than working alone.
My friends and I worked together and finished a big picture.

examples.ko: 모두 협동하지 않으면 이 게임은 이길 수 없어요.
examples.en: If we don't all cooperate, we can't win this game.

explain: '협동하다'는 학교나 놀이에서 함께 목표를 이루는 모습에 잘 어울려요. 회사 일이나 나라 사이에서는 '협력하다'를 더 많이 써요. '협동 작업', '협동심'처럼 명사로도 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: Sports day helps build a spirit of cooperation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 힘을 합치려는 마음을 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun for the spirit of working together.

phrases.en: My friends and I pooled our efforts to do the homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '협동하다'를 쉬운 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language way of saying 협동하다.

phrases.en: We made a poster through teamwork.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여럿이 나누어 함께 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for work shared and done together by several people.

explain_en: 협동하다 fits well with school or play where people reach a goal together. For business or between countries, 협력하다 is more common. You also see it in nouns like 협동 작업 and 협동심 (team spirit).

p.n: 협동 stresses close teamwork; 협력 is broader.

examples.ko: 학교 누리집 공지문을 보고서야 휴강인 걸 알았어요.
examples.en: Only after seeing the school website notice did I find out class was canceled.
The professor is sick, so today's class is canceled.

examples.ko: 내일 휴강이라서 학교에 안 가도 돼요.
examples.en: Tomorrow's class is canceled, so I don't have to go to school.

examples.ko: 휴강 공지가 늦게 올라와서 이미 도착했어요.
examples.en: The cancellation notice was posted late, so I had already arrived.
A canceled class gets a make-up session later.

examples.ko: 갑자기 휴강이 돼서 친구들이랑 카페에 갔어요.
examples.en: Class was suddenly canceled, so I went to a cafe with friends.

explain: 교수님이나 선생님 사정으로 수업을 하지 않는 것이에요. 나중에 그 수업을 채우는 것은 '보강'이라고 해요. 시간표에서 수업이 없는 시간을 말하는 '공강'과는 달라요.

phrases.en: The professor cancelled today's class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업을 쉬는 일을 동사로 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of skipping a class.

phrases.en: A class cancellation notice was posted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 누리집이나 메시지로 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for notices on the school website or by message.

phrases.en: We make up for the cancelled class next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴강한 수업을 나중에 채우는 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Making up for a cancelled class later.

explain_en: It means a class is not held because of the instructor's circumstances. Making up that class later is called '보강'. It differs from '공강', which is a free period in your timetable with no class.
